ready1_open_rewrite.title: SciVerse open question
ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: Diabetes is a disease characterized by cells being unable to correctly produce (type I) or respond (type II) to insulin. Insulin is produced by the islets and released when blood glucose levels rise; without insulin, glucose accumulates in the blood. Patients with type I diabetes usually need insulin injections. Question: After consuming which type of food do such patients most need an insulin injection?
ready1_open_rewrite.expected_answer: After consuming high-sugar foods (such as cookies)

Image description: The figure is a schematic of glycolysis and gluconeogenesis pathways, with a box labeled "Glucose" at the top, connected downward to intermediates such as fructose-6-phosphate, indicating that the metabolic pathways discussed in the figure center on glucose and changes in its level.
Reasoning: The question stem states that insulin is released when blood glucose levels rise, and that without insulin, glucose accumulates in the blood. Patients with type I diabetes cannot correctly produce insulin, so they need external injections to cope with elevated blood glucose. What most directly raises blood glucose is food that is high in sugar and easily digested into glucose, so after eating high-sugar foods such as cookies, an insulin injection is most needed.
